raw_content:
{
  "hook": "At 1,000 meters above sea level on the southern slope of the Sierra de Gredos, El Reventón forces Garnacha Tinta and Alicante Bouschet to root through fractured granite. The altitude preserves acidity while the pigmented flesh of the Alicante Bouschet injects a dense, inky structure into the old-vine Garnacha base. This is a high-elevation study in tension rather than power.",
  "wine_summary": "Rodrigo Méndez and Fernando García built Comando G around a single guiding principle: extreme altitude and granitic soils can force Garnacha into a lean, precise profile that mirrors cool-climate Pinot Noir. They farm biodynamically across scattered Cebreros plots, rejecting irrigation and synthetic inputs to let the vines struggle. The resulting wines carry a distinct mineral backbone and avoid the jammy fruit concentration that plagues lower-elevation Spanish reds. Critics consistently rate recent vintages between 94 and 97 points because the structural balance holds even in warm years like 2020.",
  "terroir_expression": "Decomposed granite and coarse quartz sand dominate the root zone, draining rapidly and forcing deep root penetration to access groundwater. The continental climate delivers scorching daytime heat followed by sharp nighttime temperature drops, which slows phenolic ripening and locks in fresh acidity. Granite contributes a flinty, saline minerality to the mid-palate, while the high site elevation stretches the growing season to develop savory herb notes instead of baked fruit.",
  "vinification_summary": "Fourteen months in neutral oak barrels strips away new-wood vanilla and allows slow micro-oxygenation to soften the Alicante Bouschet’s aggressive tannins. Whole-cluster fermentation introduces stem-derived tannins that add grip without astringency, though exact percentages shift vintage by vintage. Malolactic fermentation completes naturally in barrel, converting sharp malic acid into softer lactic acid and rounding out the mouthfeel without adding buttery flavors.",
  "food_pairing": "Serve slow-braised oxtail in a dark mole to let the wine’s grippy tannins bind with the collagen and rich protein, softening the finish. Pair with roasted chicken marinated in smoked paprika and garlic for a casual weeknight match that aligns the wine’s herbal notes with the spice rub. Try it with wild mushroom and aged Manchego risotto to bridge the wine’s earthy undertones with the cheese’s sharp, crystalline texture. Match with seared venison loin and blackberry reduction to echo the wine’s dark fruit intensity while cutting through the gamey fat. Serve alongside grilled sardines with alioli for a lighter coastal option that lets the wine’s saline minerality shine.",
  "comparable_wines": [
    "Bodegas y Viñedos Raúl Pérez Ultreia La Vitoriana — shares the same biodynamic, old-vine Garnacha focus on granitic soils in Bierzo, producing a similarly structured, acid-driven profile.",
    "Dominio de Tares PS 4 — leans heavier on Mencía but mirrors the high-altitude freshness and mineral-driven finish found in the Gredos foothills."
  ],
  "style_profile": "Medium-full bodied dry red with vibrant acidity, grippy tannins, and dark fruit intensity.",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Keeping bottles at a steady 12–14°C prevents cork degradation while slow-tannin integration continues through the 2030 vintage.",
  "value_assessment": "€65 to €85 buys you a bottle that competes directly with single-vineyard Priorat Garnacha and premium Bierzo offerings. The price reflects strict biodynamic farming, extreme site selection, and consistent critic scores above 95. You pay a premium for provenance, but the structural integrity delivers aging potential that mass-market Spanish reds lack.",
  "market_position": "Sommeliers who stock this bottle target guests seeking Spanish alternatives to red Burgundy. Restaurant wine lists feature it as a serious, age-worthy option, while independent retailers move limited allocations quickly. Collectors track specific vintages for cellar libraries, though retail turnover remains steady enough for dedicated enthusiasts to secure a few bottles annually.",
  "insider_take": "The 2020 vintage sits at 15% ABV and carries heavy tannic weight that will bruise your palate if uncorked too soon. Buying this bottle for a Tuesday night dinner misses its structural intent entirely. Hold it for at least six years or decant it aggressively if you must open a bottle now.",
  "aging_potential_years": 15,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 6,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 15,

  }
}
